text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Donors say they will not release relief funds for flood-hit areas in the lower Shire river valley until the government releases reliable statistics on flood victims.
- President Bakili Muluzi intends to meet his predecessor Kamuzu Banda for the first time since he took power in 1994, the ruling United Democratic Front said.

- Siltation and mud has affected the country's largest hydro-electric power station, causing the reservoirs to take half of the designed three million cubic metres of water, the Electricity Supply Commission's chief executive Raynord Duncan said.

- The Malawi Law Society says it will set up a commisson of inquiry to investigate reports that Chief Justice Richard Banda approached High Court judge Dunstan Mwaungulu last year to rule in favour of the government in the Press Trust Reconstruction Act (PTRA) case.
- President Muluzi is due to present the budget on March 5.

- A Blantyre-based businessman is demanding 1.5 million kwacha in compensation from the government for allegdly violating his privacy and subjecting him to mental torture when police raided his home without a search warrant after the abduction of a baby from South Africa earlier this week.
- South African police have arrived in Malawi to help search for two men who kidnapped a 14-month-old baby in South Africa last Saturday.

- The head of Malawi's Tea Factory, John Chikago -- at the centre of a row over management of the company -- has been appointed Malawi's High Commissioner to Pretoria, replacing veteran diplomat Willie Khoza.
